newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- MARCH 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- MARCH 7.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:
KATHIMERINI

--The finance ministry is to attempt to improve its lacklustre inflow performance by increasing the intensity and number of tax insepctions and cross-checks, beginning with major retailers and reports of their withholding payment of Value Added Tax.

--The National Bank of Greece believes it can raise 500 billion drachmas with the issue of new shares within 1997. The bank believes the new titles can be easily absorbed by the current demand both at home and abroad.
--Sales of motorbikes and motorcycles have increased by 53 percent in the last two months alone.
IMERISIA

--The government is taking urgent measures to turn around the disappointing course of tax revenues, as the rate for inflows for the first two months of the year is well below the forecast target of 14.6 percent.
--The dollar hit a record high against the drachma yesterday, closing at 269.750 drachmas.
--Inspired by the spirit of the Olympics, the Athens Stock Exchange's general price index closed at 1,335.60 points, up 3.36 percent, and apparently back in form.
--The finance ministry is planning an auction of multi-year bonds with fixed interest rates for March 19.
--The government is planning new road axes from the Egnatia Highway that will link Greece to the Balkans.
KERDOS
--Some 400 firms will face the tax department's spotlight on the basis of credible rumours of avoiding the payment of VAT. About half of the number are involved in wholesale trade.
--The operation of the new economic crimes squad will begin in earnest in mid-April, according to reports.
--Elviemek was placed under probation by the Athens Stock Exchange yesterday for two months, in line with a previous decision to have the public fully aware of a company's financial situation.
EXPRESS

--Businessmen who have invested in Albania are calling for compensation from the government, who they say urged them to invest in the neighbouring country and are responsible for any losses they suffer due to the political situation.
NAFTEMBORIKI

--Following drawn-out negotiations, Greece's electricity company, DEH, and Gazprom, a Russian natural gas distributor, yesterday signed a 180 billion drachma agreement for a 360 mW lignite plant in Florina.
--The national economy ministry predicts 6.3 percent inflation for March: today will see the announcement of February inflation. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
